bifrost: springboard/apps/contacts-desktop/src/contacts.rs (app-internal card and editor); springboard/src/shell/contactstore.rs (shell-internal store); springboard/src/shell/share/mod.rs (vCard item)
summary: Apple's Contacts UI is three view controllers or controls: a contact viewer, a contact picker, and a limited-access button. BifrOSt has no app-facing SDK equivalent of any of them. The Contacts app draws its own card and editor, and the contact store lives in the shell, so other apps cannot reuse either.

features.note: The Contacts app shows a contact card, but only inside that app. No SDK view controller exists for other apps to display a contact.
Editing exists in the Contacts app only. Saving happens when the form is done, and Cancel leaves the contact unchanged. Not exposed as an SDK API.

Wave 2 (contacts-ui, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. An app cannot ask the user to choose a contact and receive the result. The share picker only lists apps, so this needs a new SDK picker and a contact-selection result.

features.apple: CNContactStore-backed UI (implicit in the framework's contact views)
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/contactstore.rs (search at line 126); springboard/sdk/src/quicksearch.rs (apps index their own content)
features.note: The shell keeps contacts in a local TSV store and searches them for the Search panel. No SDK call lets an app read or search contacts through a supported API.

features.feature: Sharing a contact as a card
features.apple: CNContact share via UI (no dedicated Contacts UI class)
features.note: The shell builds a vCard 3.0 for a contact and the share menu sends it. Apps cannot create a contact card item themselves.

features.bifrost: none found; no contacts permission gate in springboard/sdk/src or springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs
features.note: Apple's button tied to the iOS and macOS limited-access permission model. BifrOSt apps have no contacts permission to request, so there is no button to match. The gap is that contact access is not gated at all.

gaps: No SDK contact picker (CNContactPicker or CNContactPickerViewController equivalent) that returns the chosen contact to an app.
No SDK contact viewer or editor view that other apps can embed; the card and editor are private to contacts-desktop.
The contact store (springboard/src/shell/contactstore.rs) is not exposed to apps through the SDK, so no app can read or search contacts.
No contacts permission model. Apps cannot request access, and there is no limited-access state to match ContactAccessButton.
docs/bifrost-ui.md has no Contacts section. springboard/README.md (Contacts section) describes only the Contacts app itself.
